title: Suchika Tariyal Wins Historic Bronze as MMA Debuts at Asian Games
excerpt: The 36-year-old lost a disputed overtime semifinal to Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon but leaves Aichi-Nagoya with India's first Asian Games medal in mixed martial arts.
body:
• Suchika Tariyal won bronze in the women's traditional -60kg MMA event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday — India's first-ever Asian Games medal in the sport.
  • The 36-year-old beat Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa 2-0 in Sunday's quarterfinal to guarantee a podium finish; both losing semifinalists receive bronze.
  • Her semifinal against Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon went to overtime and was decided on a body-weight tie-break, a verdict Tariyal openly disputed.
  • MMA is making its debut at the 2026 Asian Games, making Tariyal's medal the first of its kind for India.

Suchika Tariyal became India's first Asian Games medallist in mixed martial arts on Monday, winning bronze in the women's traditional -60kg event at the Aichi-Nagoya Games as the sport made its debut on the continental stage.

The 36-year-old from Haryana secured her place on the podium after a dramatic semifinal loss to Singapore's Teo Hui Hoon, which went to overtime and was decided on a body-weight tie-break — a verdict Tariyal openly disputed. The medal, however, stands as a landmark for Indian MMA: the first of what the country's fight community hopes will be many.

A semifinal that went down to the scales

Tariyal had guaranteed herself a medal on Sunday with a composed 2-0 quarterfinal victory over Mongolia's Altanchimeg Baigalmaa — both losing semifinalists receive bronze, so the win ensured India would appear on an MMA podium for the first time.

A day later, the semifinal against Teo was far tighter. After an even contest extended into overtime, officials ruled in favour of the Singaporean on the body-weight tie-break — the lighter athlete advances in the event of a tie. Tariyal was visibly distraught, initially hesitating to step forward for the announcement until urged on by her coaches.

Speaking to ANI after the bout, she made no secret of her frustration with the decision.

"I tried my absolute best to change the colour of this medal. But due to certain circumstances, I couldn't achieve that. I feel the decision didn't go in my favour, and I completely disagree with that verdict."

— Suchika Tariyal, speaking to ANI

"I am well aware of the rules — that in a tie, the lighter athlete wins — but a fight doesn't get decided on that basis alone," she added. "If you watch the bout, I was clearly winning. I executed all the takedowns; she didn't manage a single takedown on me."

Two decades of combat sports

The bronze is the latest milestone in a career spanning more than two decades across combat disciplines. Tariyal took up judo at 12, reportedly after an incident of eve-teasing, as self-defence. She became an eight-time national judo champion, won gold at the 2019 Commonwealth Judo Championships and the 2019 South Asian Games, and represented India in more than 20 international competitions, including the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham, where she reached the bronze-medal bout.

She then competed in kurash at the 2023 Asian Games before winning a world title in fighting jiu-jitsu in 2024.

Her MMA career has been stop-start: a professional debut win in 2017, then seven years away from the cage while pursuing judo and jiu-jitsu. She returned in late 2024, signing a multi-fight BRAVE Combat Federation contract in November and fighting at BRAVE CF 92 in Bahrain that December. The comeback followed a serious knee injury, and she also gained wider public recognition through an appearance on the reality show Roadies. Two bronze medals at the Asian MMA Championships earlier in 2026 secured her place in India's Asian Games contingent.

What it means for Indian MMA

MMA is one of several new sports debuting at Aichi-Nagoya, alongside BMX, teqball, padel, surfing and virtual taekwondo — a sign of the push toward younger audiences. India's first medal arrives as domestic MMA grows, with promoters and academies building a pipeline of fighters who previously had to look abroad for top-level competition.

For the Indian contingent, Tariyal's bronze adds to a strong opening day that also brought medals in shooting. For the fighter herself, the medal came with a measure of pride even in disappointment: as she told ANI, "While I couldn't change the colour of the medal, I am proud that I was able to win a place in the hearts of my countrymen."

What's next

Tariyal now returns to her professional MMA career with the BRAVE Combat Federation. Whether the disputed semifinal becomes a footnote or a motivator will depend on what comes next in the cage — but India's first Asian Games MMA medal is in the record books, and it belongs to her.
image_caption: Suchika Tariyal holds the Indian flag aloft after her Brave CF 92 debut victory in December 2024. The 36-year-old won bronze in the women's traditional -60kg event at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, India's first-ever MMA medal at the Games.
nri_angle: India's first Asian Games MMA medal arrives as the sport surges in global popularity, giving diaspora fight fans a homegrown name to follow on the international circuit.
